Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis?
Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)?

Does the kidney transplant recipient (KTR) have any contraindications or safety concerns for exercise (e.g., situations where traumatic damage to the transplanted kidney, participation in contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements is being considered without specialist input)?
Is the KTR currently in the immediate post-transplant period (< 1–2 days after transplantation)?
Is the patient in the pre-transplant waiting period (candidate awaiting kidney transplant)?
Is the KTR willing and able to participate in structured exercise sessions at least 3 times per week?

gold_path.conclusion: Encourage general physical activity toward 150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (or 75 minutes vigorous), aiming to reduce all‑cause and cardiovascular mortality and improve functional outcomes, and address individual barriers and activators to increase uptake; structured exercise can be advised but may be unsupervised or adapted to the patient’s circumstances.
